title: Centralize shard negotiation and lexicon sanity pass
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem: The model ingest pipeline contains multiple, overlapping shard negotiation flows and ad-hoc tokenizer boundary checks. This causes intermittent bootstrapping failures for large sharded checkpoints, inconsistent vocab checksums across loaders, and unnecessary synchronous downloads that inflate cold-start time.

Goal: Consolidate the shard negotiation protocol into a single reusable service, harmonize lexicon/vocab checksum semantics across loaders, and add a sequence-aware prefetch path for the most common segment distributions. The end result should reduce model cold-start latency, simplify upgrade paths for new weight formats, and reduce operator cognitive load when debugging load failures.

Background: Over the past 18 months we introduced multiple optimizations (lazy shard activation, streaming manifests, per-format probe hooks). Each change solved a short-term problem but accumulated protocol drift: conflicting header fields, duplicated manifest reconciliation logic, and mismatched tokenizer boundary handling that forces fallback to full-tokenizer warmups in some edge cases.

Scope: Engine + loader libraries + lightweight orchestration shim used by Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes. We will not change on-disk weight formats in this ticket; instead we will add an adapter layer and migration tests.
acceptance_criteria: Single shard negotiation code-path used by model-loader and eager/streaming activation (no duplicate negotiation logic across packages)
Vocab checksum spec (sha256 of normalized-vocab) documented and enforced by loaders; existing models validate or emit upgrade hint instead of failing silently
End-to-end cold-start median time for a representative 30B sharded checkpoint reduced by >= 12% on staging benchmarks
Sequence-aware prefetch reduces synchronous byte fetches for >80% of request shapes in the internal perf corpus
All loader regressions covered by added unit + integration tests; negative tests for tokenizer boundary fuzzing added to CI
implementation_steps: Draft canonical shard negotiation proto and lightweight in-process facade (ENG-276581-a)
Refactor existing loader modules to call the facade; remove duplicate negotiation code from format adapters (ENG-276581-b)
Implement vocab normalizer and checksum validator; add warning-mode for non-conforming manifests (ENG-276581-c)
Add sequence-aware prefetch optimizer into runtime bootstrap path with feature flag
Add end-to-end tests (unit + integration) including tokenizer boundary fuzz harness and staged activation validation
Run on staging with subset of models and measure load latencies and error rates
Roll out in canary across Hosted runtime, then Dedicated pools, monitor for anomalies
Gradually enable for Private customers by providing opt-in config and migration guide
rollback_plan: Feature flag for the canonical negotiation facade. If we observe increased errors or regressions during canary, flip the flag to revert to previous per-format negotiation. In case of manifest checksum enforcement causing customer failures, server will emit a soft-fail notice and fall back to legacy validation for that model until a follow-up hotfix is applied.

2025-09-20 - PM review (Ava Chen): Confirmed low immediate customer impact; recommend canary in Hosted first. Also requested explicit migration notes when forcing checksum validation.
2025-09-27 - Code review (PR 4821): Feedback from Marco R. - move checksum calculation into shared utils and add streaming hash API. Assigned back to ENG-276581-b for follow-up.

2025-10-01 - Diego Morales: Staging run with 30B sharded model shows cold-start median improved 13.6% and p95 improved 9.2%. Tokenizer boundary fuzz found one edge-case for legacy GPT-style merges; added a compatibility shim and test.
notes: We intentionally avoid changing on-disk weight formats in this ticket to reduce cross-team coordination overhead; a follow-up migration ticket will handle format upgrades.
Consider later exposing manifest validation results to Console as a per-model ingest health indicator.
This ticket should help reduce operational toil by centralizing logs and errors related to activation failures into a single observable span
